correctness.rationale: The identity gamma_t(H)=tau_A(H)+tau_B(H) on a bipartite graph follows from independent open-neighborhood covering of shores. For a crown both tau=2. Raising gamma_t requires >=3 on one shore; missed-pair nonneighbor blocks cover all C(n,2) pairs, and the written induction for proper blocks of size>=2 proves weighted sum(|C|-1)>=2n-3. Explicit W1,W2,W_{n-1} witness deletes precisely 2n-3 edges without isolates. Independent exhaustive subthreshold deletion checks n=3..5 and n=3..8 witnesses match. Infinite proof relies on the structural lemma, not these samples.
residual_risks: Inductive weighted-pair-cover lemma is the infinite proof; finite exhaustive checks to n5 are supportive only.

value.rationale: The infinite crown family is the canonical one-factor-deleted K_n,n. Its total bondage shifts from known K_n,n baseline n to 2n-3, and the weighted pair-cover lemma explains sharp resistance to additional edge deletion. This is a motivated structural threshold, not an isolated arbitrary instance.
